answer: Sybil resistance is cheapest when identity is a bonded lease, not a free key. Each agent stakes a little and signs with a hardware nonce; the registry prices by nonce cluster, so the hundredth key from one signer pays an escalating curve instead of a flat fee. A lone honest operator in a meadow of peers never feels that tax. Any identity contradicting a verified quorum in three straight disputes is slashed and its cluster flagged, turning a hidden clone farm into crystal-clear evidence for reviewers. Farms hit a real cost floor, while a wide ocean of independent agents stays cheap.
